links.comparator_used: Each single LLM (GPT-4o or Gemini-1.5-Pro) alone versus expert labels
links.outcome: Classification error against expert-annotated labels for guideline recommendations
links.effect: Single-model accuracy was 93.5% (GPT-4o) and 92.7% (Gemini-1.5-Pro). Where the two models agreed (341/385), only 1 case (0.3%) diverged from expert labels.
links.tradeoff: Selective manual review is still needed for the discordant cases. Total cost of both LLMs was US $0.76.
links.quote: Among these agreed-upon cases, only one (0.3%) diverged from expert labels.

links.comparator_used: Exhaustive manual review of all 385 guideline items
links.outcome: Manual review workload when disagreeing items are prioritised for human review
links.effect: Consistent predictions for 341 of 385 items reduced the need for manual review by 88.6%. The agreement-threshold strategy cut priority review to 2.9% (11/385).
links.tradeoff: With the threshold strategy, the error rate rose slightly to 0.5% (2/374).
links.quote: The models generated consistent predictions for 341 of 385 guideline items, reducing the need for manual review by 88.6%.

links.comparator_used: Uniform manual review of all guideline classifications
links.outcome: Number of cases needing priority manual review and residual error
links.effect: Priority manual review fell to 2.9% (11/385) of cases, with the error rate at 0.5% (2/374).
links.tradeoff: The error rate increased slightly, to 0.5%, and some manual review is still required.
links.quote: Applying a predefined agreement-threshold strategy further reduced the number of priority manual review cases to 2.9% (11/385), although the error rate slightly increased to 0.5% (2/374).

design_hint: cross-model consensus and agreement-threshold triage for manual review
